function: Learned frequency-plan design (reuse group, start frequency, bandwidth) and initial transmit power of each beam in a multibeam GEO high-throughput satellite (pp. 3, 6-7).
system: GEO flexible HTS, 40 beams from array antennas with digital beamforming, forward link, Ka-band 17.7-20.2 GHz, 52 dBi beam gain; no RIS (pp. 6, 11).
method: Cooperative multi-agent PPO, one fully connected actor-critic network per beam (3 hidden layers, 256 neurons), reinforcement learning; second stage is non-learned DC programming (pp. 8, 10-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space path-loss link budget (Eq. 4-5), Poisson user traffic, ITU-R S.672-4 antenna pattern, beam centres random in East Asian cities; no measured data (pp. 3, 5, 11).
test_conditions: Train: 3000 episodes, 40 beams (p. 11). Test: random demands unseen in training (p. 13), demand sweep 500-3000 Mbps (Fig. 10), 10-40 beams (Table III, p. 14).
baselines: Non-learned: random (untrained network), greedy, GA, PSO, SA; learned: multi-agent DQN, hybrid SAC; ablation: CMAPPO without the DC stage (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Average capacity matching rate, share of beams meeting demand, total beam power, interfered frequency blocks, execution time, training reward (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Training O(E*B*M*(L*K^2+A^2)), inference O(L*K^2+A^2) (p. 9); DC stage O(B*I*n^3*log(1/tau)) (p. 11); execution 35 s, 38 s with DC stage, 40 beams (p. 14).
openness: none: no code or data link; only Python 3.8, PyTorch and CVX are named (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "(6) is a typical satellite communication link budget method"; the channel is free-space path loss plus gains and losses (Eq. 4-5), and the beam pattern follows ITU-R S.672-4 (p. 11). Missing: no 3GPP TR 38.811 or other standard channel model, no measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "were randomly generated within a certain range and were not used during the training phase"; these are held-out demand draws of the same simulator, and p. 12 says the policy is "tailored to that specific distribution". Missing: no new scenario, band, beam count or site tested with a trained model, no adaptation reported.
q3_support: p. 14: "Fig. 10 shows the average capacity matching rate of different algorithms"; non-learned GA, PSO, SA and greedy (p. 12), learned "Multi-Agent DQN" (pp. 12-13) and "Hybrid Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)" (p. 13), both applied to the same problem.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the application phase is" O(L x K^2 + A^2), with the training phase O(E x B x M x (L x K^2 + A^2)); p. 11: IODCP O(B x I x n^3 log(1/tau)); p. 14: "Table III presents the execution time of different algorithms".
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulation results of the first stage CMAPPO framework were obtained in Python 3.8 environment using PyTorch-GPU"; p. 15: "validate the proposed two-stage optimization framework using real-world operational data" is future work. Missing: no code or data link, no public or measured dataset.
notes: Area 6: learned control of beam power, bandwidth and frequency plan of a satellite link is physical layer, so above_phy does not apply. The second stage (IODCP, p. 10) is classical DC programming, so CMAPPO alone is an ablation and not a baseline. q1: ITU-R S.672-4 is cited only as the antenna radiation pattern (p. 11), not as a channel model; the reviewer may confirm. q2: the Fig. 9 demands (p. 13) are random draws of the same simulator; the paper does not say whether Fig. 10 and Table III (10-40 beams) reuse one trained network or retrain, so it is scored 0. The text announces five benchmarks but lists seven (p. 12).
